local_checks.result: _holders (trusted_exec_contract.py:221-264) lists /proc (:238), lists each pid's fd directory (:242), stats each /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> link (:252), and reads /proc/<pid>/status, comm and cmdline as bytes for a matching pid only (:231-235, :257-260). os.stat follows the magic link to the open file's inode without opening it, and the three reads are procfs files, never the sentinel, so the scan cannot be a reader the probe counts. It runs from _attempt while the probe's own writer is open and skips exactly that descriptor of its own pid (:248-249, :280), before the writer closes (:282); a host without /proc gets a fixed text (:227-228). Another user's process is skipped on PermissionError and only counted (:243-245), so the scan reaches only processes of the user the tests run as, the same principal, and only those holding the sentinel.

local_checks.invariant: the record of another process's command line reaches only readers that may see it, in a form that cannot act as anything but text
local_checks.result: Holds for the boundary, recorded as hardening for the form: a holder's comm and first 200 characters of its cmdline, NULs turned to spaces and nothing else escaped (:259-260), enter self.reads and the AssertionError of assert_untouched (:280, :344), so they reach the test's output: the operator's terminal on a local run and the CI log of the test cell. The process named is one of the tests' user that holds a FIFO under the test's own temporary worker root, normally the consumer under test (repository code), so its argv is the tests' own. No principal above that user is read, and the pull request's author already controls every byte the test prints. A newline or `::` in a holder's argv would still reach the log raw, and a token passed as argv to a process that opened the sentinel would be printed (GitHub masks only registered secrets).

hardening: WorkerRoot._holders puts a holder's comm and the first 200 characters of its cmdline into the failure message unescaped (tests/unit/trusted_exec_contract.py:259-260, raised at :344), so a control character, a newline followed by a `::` workflow command, or an argv-borne token of a process that opened the sentinel reaches the terminal or the CI log as written. The reader is the tests' own user and the named process holds the test's own FIFO, so no boundary is crossed; formatting the fields with repr() (or escaping everything outside printable ASCII) and printing argv[0] with the argument count instead of the arguments would keep the record useful without carrying another process's arguments into a log.
